blocks.content: Scaling a StatefulSet respects the same ordering principle covered in the previous topic, scaling up follows the same ascending creation order, but scaling down runs in strict reverse, removing the highest-numbered replica first.
1. Scaling Up: the Same Ordered Creation
blocks.text: 1. Scaling Up: the Same Ordered Creation

blocks.content: Increasing a StatefulSet's replica count follows exactly the same rule as initial creation, covered in the Ordered Deployment topic, new replicas are added one at a time, in ascending order, each waiting for the previous to be ready.

blocks.alt: The same ascending, one-at-a-time creation, just triggered by scaling up

blocks.content: Scaling down does not remove replicas arbitrarily, it removes them in exactly the reverse order, the highest-numbered replica goes first, working its way back down, never the other way around.

blocks.alt: The exact reverse order, highest ordinal removed first, always

blocks.content: 3. Never a Gap in the Middle
blocks.text: 3. Never a Gap in the Middle

blocks.content: This ordering guarantee means a StatefulSet never ends up with, say, app-0 removed while app-1 and app-2 still exist, the set of existing replicas is always a contiguous, unbroken range starting from app-0.

blocks.alt: Always a contiguous, unbroken set of replicas, never a gap in the middle

blocks.content: This predictability avoids a genuinely thorny problem, ambiguity about which replica holds a special role (a primary or leader, for instance), consistent, ordered removal means the system never has to reason about an unpredictable, arbitrary set of surviving replicas.

blocks.alt: Avoiding real ambiguity about which replica remains and in what role

blocks.content: A Deployment scaling down, covered in its own module, has no such guarantee, any replica can be removed, since they are all interchangeable, StatefulSet's reverse-order scaling exists precisely because its replicas are not interchangeable at all.

blocks.alt: No such guarantee needed for Deployment, since its replicas are interchangeable

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Scaling up follows the same ordered creation as initial deployment, scaling down runs in strict reverse, always removing the highest-numbered replica first.
This guarantees a StatefulSet's existing replicas always form a contiguous range from app-0, avoiding real ambiguity about which replica holds a special role.
